guide.summary: A colony stuck to a surface that pushes back rival microbes with a chemical.
guide.biology: Some bacteria living on surfaces release chemicals that slow down competing microbes nearby.
guide.rules: Must attach to gel, sediment, mesh or a stone edge and never moves. Eats sugar first, then metabolite, using oxygen. When an active Sprinter, Brinecoil or Sourbud is within 2 cells, it has more than 50 energy and local rivalry is below 1.0, it releases rivalry chemical at 0.02 per second for 0.60 energy per second. Rivalry harms only those three kinds, adding a quarter of its level to their inhibitor exposure, and gives Rampart no direct bonus.
guide.example: Grow Ramparts on a stone edge beside a sugar patch, add Sprinters, and compare how Sprinters fare near and far from the colony.
